These isotopes are used in positron emission tomography, an important medical imaging technique described in the Connection to Medicine.

Electron capture is another process by which proton-rich nuclei decay, converting a proton to a neutron; it is an important alternative when energetic considerations don’t allow positron emission (see Section 19.3). The nucleus captures an orbital electron, thereby converting a proton into a neutron, as shown in Figure 19.8.
